questions.q: Fill up: The causative organism printed is ____ tuberculosis.
questions.exp: Page 188 names 'Causative organism (mycobacterium tuberculosis)'.

questions.q: The primary source of infection is printed as:
questions.exp: '1° source: Lung > LNs'.

questions.q: Fill up: The classic route of spread to the genital tract is ____.
questions.exp: 'Hematogenous route' heads the pathogenesis flow.

questions.q: Which second, less common route is printed?
questions.exp: 'Transmission: Sexual' appears in the diagram.

questions.q: Fill up: The organism enters and first involves the ____ tube.
questions.exp: 'Enters Fallopian Tube (FT)'.

questions.q: How is the tubal lining destroyed?
questions.exp: 'Lining destroyed from within → Endosalpingitis'.

questions.q: Fill up: In genital tuberculosis the tubal lining is destroyed from within, producing ____.
questions.exp: The chain prints 'Endosalpingitis → Caseous necrosis → Fibrosis/Adhesion'.

questions.q: Which three pathological stages follow endosalpingitis?
questions.exp: The printed sequence is caseous necrosis then fibrosis or adhesion.

questions.q: Fill up: The tubal damage culminates in ____ cornual block.
questions.exp: 'B/L cornual block'.

questions.q: From the uterus the infection spreads to the:
questions.exp: 'From uterus: Spreads to Endometrium'.

questions.q: Fill up: Fimbrial spread causes adhesions and ____.
questions.exp: 'Fimbriae spread: Causes adhesions, Causes hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Match each step of the tubal pathogenesis with its position - 1) Lining destroyed from within 2) Caseous necrosis 3) Fibrosis or adhesion 4) Bilateral cornual block ... A) 4 B) 1 C) 3 D) 2
questions.exp: The flow is endosalpingitis, caseous necrosis, fibrosis or adhesion, then bilateral cornual block.

questions.q: Scenario: A young woman with infertility is found to have bilateral cornual block on HSG. Which organism does the printed pathogenesis point to?
questions.exp: Bilateral cornual block is the end point of the genital tuberculosis tubal chain.

questions.q: True/False: The fallopian tube is the first genital structure involved because the organism reaches it by the haematogenous route.
opts: False - the ovary is involved first
False - the endometrium is involved first
questions.exp: The diagram shows haematogenous seeding entering the fallopian tube first.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed route or source in the pathogenesis diagram?
questions.exp: Ascending spread along sperms belongs to PID and cervicitis, not genital tuberculosis.

questions.q: Fill up: Genital tuberculosis of the tube is ____ (bilateral or unilateral).
questions.exp: The sites block prints 'B/L'.

questions.q: Which part of the tube is most commonly affected?
questions.exp: 'm/c site: Ampulla > Isthmus'.

questions.q: The most common presentation is:
questions.exp: 'm/c presentation: Infertility'.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for tubal patency is ____.
questions.exp: 'IOC for tubal patency: HSG (Hysterosalpingography)'.

questions.q: Why is HSG contraindicated in untreated genital tuberculosis?
questions.exp: '- C/I: Can lead to dissemination'.

questions.q: When is HSG performed in genital tuberculosis?
questions.exp: '- Done after ATT (Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment)'.

questions.q: How many characteristic appearances on HSG are printed?
questions.exp: Beaded, lead pipe, tobacco pouch, golf stick, bilateral cornual block, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx.

questions.q: Which three HSG appearances are illustrated with labelled figures?
opts: Beaded appearance, tobacco pouch appearance and lead pipe appearance
Golf stick, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx
Beaded, golf stick and cornual block
Lead pipe, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx
questions.exp: The figures are captioned beaded appearance, tobacco pouch appearance and lead pipe appearance.

questions.q: Fill up: The appearance resembling a smoking pipe is called the ____ appearance.
questions.exp: 'Tobacco pouch appearance'.

questions.q: Which appearance is described as a golf stick?
questions.exp: The printed item is 'Golfstick appearance'.

questions.q: Fill up: A fluffy, ill-defined outline on HSG is the ____ appearance.
questions.exp: 'Cotton wool appearance'.

questions.q: The 'lead pipe' appearance describes a tube that is:
questions.exp: The lead pipe appearance is the rigid, pipe-like outline of a fibrosed tube.

questions.q: Match each HSG appearance with its descriptor - 1) Beaded 2) Lead pipe 3) Tobacco pouch 4) Cotton wool ... A) Rigid pipe-like tube B) Fluffy ill-defined outline C) Sac-like distal collection D) Alternating constrictions and dilatations
questions.exp: Beaded is alternating constrictions; lead pipe is rigid; tobacco pouch is a distal sac; cotton wool is fluffy.

questions.q: Scenario: A patient with suspected genital tuberculosis needs tubal assessment. What is the correct printed sequence?
opts: Start anti-tuberculous treatment first, then perform HSG
Perform HSG and then decide on treatment
Perform laparoscopy instead, as HSG is never used
questions.exp: HSG is contraindicated before treatment because of dissemination risk and is done after ATT.

questions.q: True/False: HSG is the investigation of choice for tubal patency and is safe at any stage of genital tuberculosis.
opts: True - it is safe after the first month
True - dissemination only occurs with laparoscopy
questions.exp: It is contraindicated before treatment because it can disseminate infection.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed HSG appearance in genital tuberculosis?
questions.exp: Violin string adhesions belong to Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome in the PID chapter.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Fill up: In genital tuberculosis of the uterus, the ____ layers of the endometrium are affected.
questions.exp: 'Affected: Superficial layers of endometrium'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Which layer is spared?
questions.exp: 'Spared: myometrium'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Fill up: Because only the superficial layers are involved, ____ day menstrual blood can be used for investigation.
questions.exp: '1st day menstrual blood can be used for Investigation'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Which phase is printed as the best time for endometrial biopsy?
questions.exp: 'Best time for endometrial biopsy: premenstrual'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Initially, when the endometrium is still normal, the menstrual pattern is:
questions.exp: 'Initially: endometrium normal → No menstrual symptoms'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Fill up: In the acute stage, endometritis causes ____.
questions.exp: 'Acute: Endometritis → menorrhagia'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: In the chronic stage, adhesions produce:
opts: Asherman syndrome with secondary amenorrhoea or oligomenorrhoea
questions.exp: 'Chronic: Adhesions (Asherman syndrome) → 2° amenorrhea/oligomenorrhea'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Fill up: Ovarian tuberculosis is limited to the surface of the ovary by the tunica ____.
questions.exp: 'TB limited to: Surface of ovary by Tunica albuginea → Prevents spread to stroma'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: What keeps ovarian tuberculosis confined to the surface?
opts: The tunica albuginea prevents spread to the stroma
The ovary has no lymphatic supply
questions.exp: The printed mechanism is the tunica albuginea blocking stromal spread.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Fill up: On laparoscopy the ovary shows ____ on its surface.
questions.exp: 'Appearance: Tubercles on surface of ovary (on laparoscopy)'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Tubercular peritonitis associated with genital tuberculosis produces:
questions.exp: 'Genital TB associated with peritonitis → Ascites'.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Match each site with its printed feature - 1) Tube 2) Uterus 3) Ovary 4) Peritoneum ... A) Ascites B) Tubercles on the surface C) Ampulla most common D) Myometrium spared
questions.exp: Tube: ampulla; uterus: myometrium spared; ovary: surface tubercles; peritoneum: ascites.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Scenario: A woman with genital tuberculosis develops secondary amenorrhoea. Which printed mechanism explains it?
opts: Chronic endometrial adhesions producing Asherman syndrome
questions.exp: The chronic uterine stage produces adhesions (Asherman syndrome) with secondary amenorrhoea.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: True/False: Genital tuberculosis typically destroys the myometrium.
opts: True - the myometrium is the main target
questions.exp: Only the superficial endometrium is affected and the myometrium is spared.

questions.sec: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.unit: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum
questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed site feature of genital tuberculosis?
opts: Cervical ulceration as the commonest finding
questions.exp: The common presentations are tubal; cervical ulceration is not printed as the commonest finding.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common age group affected is ____ years.
questions.exp: 'm/c age group: 20-30 years'.

questions.q: Genital tuberculosis is the most common cause of PID in:
questions.exp: 'm/c cause of PID in virgin females'.

questions.q: Fill up: The fever of genital tuberculosis is described as ____ grade.
questions.exp: 'Prodromal Symptoms: Fever (Low grade)'.

questions.q: Which three prodromal symptoms are printed?
opts: Low grade fever, malaise and loss of appetite with weight loss
questions.exp: The prodromal list is fever, malaise and decreased appetite with weight loss.

questions.q: Fill up: The commonest presentation is infertility due to ____ blockage.
questions.exp: 'm/c: Infertility d/t Tubal blockage'.

questions.q: Initially the menstrual abnormality is:
questions.exp: 'Initially: menorrhagia d/t endometritis'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common menstrual abnormality is secondary ____ or hypomenorrhoea.
questions.exp: 'm/c: 2° amenorrhea / hypomenorrhea d/t Asherman syndrome'.

questions.q: Which pain symptom is marked as variable?
questions.exp: '± Chronic pelvic pain' uses the plus-minus sign.

questions.q: Fill up: The rare discharge is described as ____ (blood stained).
questions.exp: 'Rare: Serosanguinous (Blood stained) discharge'.

questions.q: Which future risk is flagged?
questions.exp: 'Future risk of: ectopic pregnancy'.

questions.q: Match each clinical item with its descriptor - 1) Infertility 2) Menorrhagia 3) Secondary amenorrhoea 4) Serosanguinous discharge ... A) Most common menstrual abnormality B) Rare C) Initial menstrual abnormality D) Most common presentation
questions.exp: Infertility is the commonest presentation; menorrhagia is initial; secondary amenorrhoea becomes commonest; the discharge is rare.

questions.q: Scenario: An 18-year-old virgin presents with pelvic inflammatory disease that has not responded to broad-spectrum antibiotics. Which diagnosis should be considered?
questions.exp: Genital TB is the commonest cause of PID in virgins and is flagged in the diagnostic history list.

questions.q: True/False: Genital tuberculosis most commonly presents with menorrhagia.
opts: True - bleeding is the cardinal symptom
questions.exp: Infertility is the commonest presentation; menorrhagia is only the initial menstrual change.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed prodromal symptom?
questions.exp: Haemoptysis is a pulmonary symptom, not in the printed prodromal list.

questions.q: Fill up: On per-abdominal examination the abdomen is described as ____.
questions.exp: 'P/A examination: Doughy abdomen' with ascites.

questions.q: Which per-speculum finding is printed?
opts: Ulcers on the cervix, vagina or vulva
questions.exp: 'P/S examination: Ulcers on cervix / vagina / vulva'.

questions.q: Fill up: On per-vaginal examination, mobility is restricted - the ____ pelvis.
questions.exp: 'Restricted mobility: Frozen pelvis'.

questions.q: Which pelvic finding is noted on per-vaginal examination?
questions.exp: 'P/V examination: Adnexal mass' with restricted mobility.

questions.q: Which two historical clues are printed first under diagnosis?
opts: Past history of tuberculosis and family history of tuberculosis
questions.exp: 'History: Past H/o TB, Family H/o TB'.

questions.q: Fill up: Chronic PID that is unresponsive to ____ antibiotics suggests tuberculosis.
questions.exp: 'Chronic PID: Unresponsive to broad spectrum antibiotics'.

questions.q: Which demographic clue in the history list is printed?
opts: PID in young or pubertal females
questions.exp: 'PID in young / pubertal females'.

questions.q: Fill up: Endometrial biopsy is taken from the ____, on both sides.
questions.exp: 'Sample site: Cornua (B/L)'.

questions.q: In which phase is the endometrial sample taken?
questions.exp: 'Phase: Premenstrual phase'.

questions.q: Fill up: In virgins, endometrial biopsy is avoided and ____ day menstrual blood is taken instead.
questions.exp: 'Virgins: Endometrial biopsy should not be done. Take 1st day menstrual blood'.

questions.q: Which medium is the biopsy sample sent in for culture?
questions.exp: '- Culture: In saline' is printed in the sample list.

questions.q: Which test is described as confirmative?
questions.exp: '- PCR: Confirmative' is printed; NAAT is listed separately.

questions.q: How is the histological diagnosis described?
questions.exp: '- Histological Diagnosis: In formation'.

questions.q: Which two ultrasound findings are printed alongside pelvic mass?
questions.exp: 'USG: Tubal dilatation, Pyosalpinx, Pelvic mass'.

questions.q: Fill up: On laparoscopy the fallopian tubes appear red and ____.
questions.exp: '1. Fallopian Tube: Red-hyperemic, Swollen, Dilated'.

questions.q: How many laparoscopic sites are listed?
questions.exp: Fallopian tube, ovary and peritoneum.

questions.q: Fill up: The purpose of taking a sample at laparoscopy is to ____ the diagnosis.
questions.exp: 'Take sample → To confirm'.

questions.q: Match each specimen with its test - 1) Culture 2) NAAT 3) PCR 4) Histopathology ... A) In saline B) Nucleic acid amplification C) Confirmative D) In formation
questions.exp: Culture goes in saline; NAAT amplifies nucleic acid; PCR is confirmative; histology is in formation.

questions.q: Scenario: A virgin girl is suspected of having genital tuberculosis. Which diagnostic specimen is appropriate?
questions.exp: In virgins the biopsy is avoided and first day menstrual blood is used.

questions.q: True/False: The endometrial biopsy in suspected genital tuberculosis is taken in the early proliferative phase.
questions.exp: The premenstrual phase is the printed timing.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed laparoscopic finding?
questions.exp: Violin string adhesions are the Fitz-Hugh-Curtis finding in the PID chapter.

questions.q: Fill up: Anti-tuberculous treatment is given as Category ____ for six months.
questions.exp: 'ATT (Category I × 6 months)'.

questions.q: For how many months is ATT given?
questions.exp: 'Category I × 6 months'.

questions.q: Fill up: The printed note says ATT can improve ____.
questions.exp: ': Can improve fertility' follows the ATT entry.

questions.q: Which procedure is printed for Asherman syndrome?
questions.exp: 'Asherman Syndrome: Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis'.

questions.q: Fill up: After adhesiolysis, a ____ Foley's catheter is placed in the cavity.
questions.exp: 'Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis + Pediatric Foley's Catheter'.

questions.q: Which hormonal regimen follows adhesiolysis and for how long?
opts: Estrogen plus progesterone for three months
Combined oral contraceptive for one year
questions.exp: '(Estrogen + Progesterone) × 3 months'.

questions.q: Fill up: For infertility with distorted pelvic anatomy or tubal block, the treatment offered is ____.
questions.exp: 'Infertility: IVF + pelvic anatomy distorted / Tubal block'.

questions.q: How many rows does the management table have?
questions.exp: TB, Asherman syndrome and infertility.

questions.q: Match each problem with its management - 1) Genital TB 2) Asherman syndrome 3) Infertility with tubal block ... A) IVF B) Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis with paediatric Foley catheter and estrogen plus progesterone for 3 months C) ATT Category I for 6 months
questions.exp: TB gets ATT; Asherman gets adhesiolysis and hormones; blocked tubes get IVF.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with treated genital tuberculosis has Asherman syndrome with secondary amenorrhoea. What is the printed management?
opts: Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis, paediatric Foley catheter and estrogen plus progesterone for three months
questions.exp: That three-part regimen is the printed Asherman syndrome row.

questions.q: True/False: The management table recommends tubal reconstructive surgery for blocked tubes in genital tuberculosis.
opts: True - if the patient is under 30
questions.exp: IVF is the printed option when pelvic anatomy is distorted or the tubes are blocked.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT part of the printed genital tuberculosis management?
opts: ATT Category I for six months
questions.exp: Culpotomy drainage belongs to the PID chapter.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Fill up: The chapter opens with the pathological heading ____.
questions.exp: The first heading on page 188 is 'PATHOGENESIS'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: How is the genital lesion categorised relative to the primary focus?
opts: It is a secondary implant from the bowel
It is a reactivation of a genital focus acquired at birth
It is a primary genital focus seeded from a lung or nodal source
It spreads contiguously from the kidney
questions.exp: The diagram labels it '1° Genital TB' with the primary source being lung greater than lymph nodes.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Fill up: The transmission block lists haematogenous spread as the main route and ____ transmission as the other.
questions.exp: 'Transmission: Sexual' is the second route printed.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Which statement best summarises the tubal sequence?
opts: Salpingitis, then pyosalpinx, then hydrosalpinx, then recanalisation
Endosalpingitis, then caseous necrosis, then fibrosis or adhesion, then bilateral cornual block
questions.exp: That is the exact printed chain on page 188.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Fill up: The two structures commonly involved are labelled ____, meaning the disease is bilateral.
questions.exp: 'SITES: B/L'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Which site within the tube is second most common after the ampulla?
questions.exp: 'm/c site: Ampulla > Isthmus'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Why is HSG deferred until after anti-tuberculous treatment?
opts: The tubes are too narrowed to cannulate before treatment
It gives a false negative before treatment
Contrast injection into an untreated tuberculous tube can disseminate the infection
questions.exp: The printed contraindication is the risk of dissemination.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Fill up: ATT is expanded as anti-____ treatment in this chapter.
questions.exp: '- Done after ATT (Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment)'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Which HSG finding represents complete proximal occlusion?
questions.exp: 'B/L cornual block' is the proximal occlusion pattern.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Match each HSG term with its place in the printed list - 1) a 2) d 3) e 4) g ... A) Cotton wool appearance B) B/L cornual block C) Beaded appearance D) Golfstick appearance
questions.exp: The printed order is a beaded, b lead pipe, c tobacco pouch, d golfstick, e B/L cornual block, f cotton wool, g hydrosalpinx.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Scenario: An HSG in a treated patient shows a rigid, pipe-like tube with a sac-like distal swelling. Which two printed appearances are present?
opts: Lead pipe appearance and tobacco pouch appearance
questions.exp: A rigid tube is the lead pipe appearance and a distal sac is the tobacco pouch appearance.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: True/False: The golfstick appearance is listed among the HSG findings of genital tuberculosis.
opts: False - it belongs to uterine anomalies
questions.exp: It is printed as item d in the HSG list.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Pathogenesis, Sites and HSG
questions.q: Odd one out - which HSG term is NOT a printed genital tuberculosis appearance?
questions.exp: The cogwheel sign is an ultrasound sign of PID.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Fill up: The significance line states that first day menstrual ____ can be used for investigation.
questions.exp: '1st day menstrual blood can be used for Investigation'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Why can first day menstrual blood be used instead of a biopsy sample?
opts: The superficial endometrial layers are shed in the menstrual flow
Menstrual blood is sterile and easy to culture
questions.exp: Because only the superficial endometrium is affected, the shed superficial layer carries the organism.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Fill up: The chronic uterine lesion is named ____ syndrome.
questions.exp: 'Chronic: Adhesions (Asherman syndrome)'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Which structure prevents spread of ovarian tuberculosis into the stroma?
questions.exp: 'TB limited to: Surface of ovary by Tunica albuginea'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Fill up: Ovarian tuberculosis is visible at laparoscopy as ____ on the ovarian surface.
questions.exp: 'Appearance: Tubercles on surface of ovary (on laparoscopy)'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Which age qualifier is attached to the 20 to 30 year peak?
opts: It is never seen before menarche
It may also be seen in young girls
It is limited to parous women
questions.exp: '± Seen in young girls' is printed beside the age group.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Fill up: The menstrual abnormality that becomes most common is secondary amenorrhoea or ____.
questions.exp: 'm/c: 2° amenorrhea / hypomenorrhea d/t Asherman syndrome'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Which single symptom is described as rare?
questions.exp: 'Rare: Serosanguinous (Blood stained) discharge'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Fill up: Genital tuberculosis carries a future risk of ____ pregnancy.
questions.exp: 'Future risk of: ectopic pregnancy'.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Match each clinical feature with its frequency tag - 1) Infertility 2) Chronic pelvic pain 3) Serosanguinous discharge 4) Prodromal fever ... A) Rare B) Most common C) Plus-minus D) Low grade
questions.exp: Infertility is most common; pelvic pain carries the plus-minus sign; the discharge is rare; fever is low grade.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Scenario: A 26-year-old woman presents with infertility and a 2-year history of low grade fever, malaise and weight loss. Which combination points to genital tuberculosis?
opts: Prodromal constitutional symptoms plus infertility from tubal blockage
Cyclical pain plus a bulging hymen
questions.exp: Low grade fever, malaise and weight loss are the printed prodrome with infertility as the commonest presentation.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: True/False: Genital tuberculosis is the commonest cause of PID in postmenopausal women.
questions.exp: It is the commonest cause in virgin females; menopausal PID is listed with E. coli.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Uterine, Ovarian and Clinical Features
questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed clinical feature?
questions.exp: Anosmia belongs to Kallmann syndrome in the primary amenorrhoea chapter.

questions.q: Fill up: The per-abdominal sign that accompanies tubercular peritonitis is a ____ abdomen with ascites.
questions.exp: 'P/A examination: Doughy abdomen, Ascites'.

questions.q: Which examination reveals the frozen pelvis?
questions.exp: 'P/V examination: Adnexal mass, Restricted mobility: Frozen pelvis'.

questions.q: Fill up: Which three specimens of the endometrial sample are listed - culture in saline, NAAT and ____?
questions.exp: The sample list is culture, NAAT, PCR and histopathology.

questions.q: Which ultrasound finding suggests acute suppuration rather than a chronic fibrosed tube?
questions.exp: 'USG: Tubal dilatation, Pyosalpinx, Pelvic mass'.

questions.q: Fill up: Laparoscopy lists three sites: fallopian tube, ovary and ____.
questions.exp: 'Site: 1. Fallopian Tube, 2. Ovary, 3. Peritoneum'.

questions.q: Which three descriptors are printed for the tuberculous tube at laparoscopy?
opts: Red and hyperaemic, swollen and dilated
questions.exp: 'Red-hyperemic, Swollen, Dilated'.

questions.q: Fill up: The management table's first row is anti-tuberculous treatment, category ____ for six months.
questions.exp: 'ATT (Category I × 6 months)'.

questions.q: What follows hysteroscopic adhesiolysis in the printed regimen?
opts: An intrauterine device and six months of estrogen
A paediatric Foley catheter and three months of estrogen plus progesterone
A second look hysteroscopy at one week
questions.exp: The Asherman row prints the catheter and the three-month hormone course.

questions.q: Fill up: Hormonal therapy after adhesiolysis is estrogen plus ____ for three months.
questions.exp: '(Estrogen + Progesterone) × 3 months'.

questions.q: Match each management row with its goal - 1) ATT 2) Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis with catheter and hormones 3) IVF ... A) Restore the cavity and prevent re-adhesion B) Treat infection and possibly improve fertility C) Bypass distorted anatomy or tubal block
questions.exp: ATT treats infection; adhesiolysis restores the cavity; IVF bypasses the tubes.

questions.q: Scenario: A treated patient has persistent tubal block and distorted pelvic anatomy. What does the table advise?
opts: Repeat ATT for six more months
questions.exp: Infertility with distorted anatomy or tubal block is the IVF row.

questions.q: True/False: Endometrial biopsy is taken from the cornua because the disease preferentially affects the cornual endometrium.
opts: False - the lower segment is preferred
questions.exp: The printed sample site is the cornua, on both sides.

questions.q: Odd one out - which diagnostic item is NOT in the printed work-up?
opts: Endometrial biopsy in the premenstrual phase
questions.exp: The Mantoux test is not printed in this chapter's work-up.

questions.q: Fill up: In a virgin with suspected genital tuberculosis, the endometrial biopsy is ____.
questions.exp: 'Virgins: Endometrial biopsy should not be done. Take 1st day menstrual blood'.

questions.q: Which two findings make the clinician suspect tuberculosis rather than ordinary PID?
opts: Chronic PID unresponsive to broad-spectrum antibiotics, and PID in a young or pubertal female
Fever above 101 degrees Fahrenheit and a raised CRP
Cervical motion tenderness and mucopurulent discharge
questions.exp: Both historical clues are printed in the diagnosis list.
